parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish فانتی (fanti), from Greek φάντης (fántis, “jack”), from Italian fante (“infantryman; knave, jack”).
Borrowed from Greek φασαρία (fasaría, “unwanted noise”) from Italian fesseria (“stupidity, nonsense”).
Inherited from Ottoman Turkish رادیكیه (radikiye), from Greek ραδίκια (radíkia), plural form of ραδίκι (radíki, “chicory”), ultimately from Italian radicchio.
From Ottoman Turkish صالچه (salça, “sauce, gravy”), from Greek σάλτσα (sáltsa), from Italian salsa. Doublet of sos and salsa, from Vulgar Latin.

parole.significato: fender, any cushion-like object, made of rubber, wood, or fibres of old rope, that is placed along the sides of a boat…
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوستورماچه (usturmaça, “fender”), from Greek στρομάτσα (stromátsa), variant of στρομάτσο (stromátso, “fender”), from Italian stramazzo (“straw mattress, pallet”), perhaps under the influence of στρώμα (stróma, “mattress”).
From Ottoman Turkish ورنیك (vernik), itself from Greek βερνίκη (verníki) or Italian vernice.

parole.significato: distaff, rock, a device to which a bundle of fibres are attached for temporary storage, before being spun
parole.testo: Inherited from Ottoman Turkish اوركه (öreke, “distaff”), from Greek ρόκα (róka, “distaff”), ultimately from Italian rocca (“distaff”).
